findings.title: website_name bypasses untrusted_attributes, exposing TL0 users' websites to anonymous viewers
findings.body:
`website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is omitted when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor). This anti-spam control exists to keep new users' links off public pages.

The new `website_name` attribute carries the website's host and often its full path, but it is not added to `untrusted_attributes` and has no equivalent guard. It is therefore always serialized.

Before this change, the client derived the display name from `model.website`, which was absent in this case, so nothing was shown. Now `user.hbs` checks `model.website_name` and renders it (as a span, because `linkWebsite` is false for TL0). Spam profiles' domains are again shown to anonymous users and crawlers.

Fix: add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`, or have its include method return false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing `?` and is never called
findings.body:
ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_<attr>?` to decide whether to emit an attribute. The method here is named `include_website_name`, without the `?`, so the serializer never calls it.

As a result `website_name` is always emitted, as `nil` when no website is set. The intended conditional inclusion never takes effect.

This also suggests the author expected this method to gate the attribute; it does not, which contributes to the untrusted-attribute leak above. It should be renamed `include_website_name?` and should also respect `restrict_user_fields?`.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic treats unrelated domains under a shared public suffix as the same site
findings.body:
When both hosts have the same number of labels and more than two, the code drops the first label of each and compares the rest. It ignores public suffixes.

For example, with the forum at `forum.co.uk`, a user website `evil.co.uk/whatever` matches on `co.uk`. Likewise `alice.github.io` vs `forum.github.io` matches on `github.io`.

In these cases unrelated third-party sites are shown with their full path, which is the opposite of what the feature intends. The comparison is also case-sensitive, so `Example.com` would not match `example.com`.

findings.title: Untrusted-attributes spec not updated for website_name; sibling-subdomain branch untested
findings.body:
The TL0/anonymous spec checks a fixed list of untrusted attributes, and `website_name` was not added to it. As a result the leak of the website host/path for TL0 users goes undetected.

Separately, the new specs only cover the exact-match, unrelated-domain and parent-domain cases. The `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` sibling-subdomain branch on line 146 has no test, nor does the case where the URL cannot be parsed or has no host.
